items.title: Ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks, Modi speaks to Zelenskyy; Jaishankar speaks to Lavrov
points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

File | Photo Credit: ANI India is ready to mediate between Russia and Ukraine to establish “food corridors”, announced Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, welcoming the offer after a telephone call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, ahead of the…
Jaishankar and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, in the clearest indication thus far of the mediatory role that New Delhi is now playing between Moscow and Kyiv.

On Tuesday, U.S. President Donald Trump’s negotiators, including his son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff, will restart negotiations after three months with Russian and Ukrainian representatives to discuss security guarantees required…
The calls from New Delhi came just ahead of the talks in the UAE, and a week before Mr. Modi and Mr. Trump are expected to meet on the sidelines of the ASEAN-linked summits in Manila.

items.title: Five persons, including four girls, drown in irrigation tank in Tiruvannamalai
points: Collector Vandhana Garg and Superintendent of Police R.

Uthayakumar during their inspection of the irrigation tank on Monday. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement A staff nurse and four girls of a government-recognised children’s home for girls drowned in an irrigation tank at Samuthiram village here on Monday…
The deceased were identified as staff nurse Thenmozhi, 24, Vijayalakshmi, 14, Alli, 14, Poomika, 13, and Valliammal, 16.
Except Valliammal, who belongs to Kilpennathur village, the other three girls are siblings from Karapattu village near Chengam.
On Monday afternoon, Thenmozhi, along with around 13 girls, went to the irrigation tank on Perumbakkam Main Road to bathe.
Hearing the other girls’ shouts, the area’s residents rushed to the spot and alerted the Tiruvannamalai West police and firefighters.
Firefighters retrieved the bodies and sent them to the Government Medical College and Hospital in Tiruvannamalai town for a post-mortem.
Uthayakumar met the families of the deceased at the hospital in the presence of hospital dean Edvina Vasantah and inspected the irrigation tank.

items.title: APSDRF rescues eight, evacuates 341 during Cyclone Arnab relief efforts
points: DGP Harish Kumar Gupta presenting rewards to the APSDRF personnel at the AP Police Headquarters in Mangalagiri on Monday. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response Force (APSDRF) shifted 341 people to safe places, rescued…
Inspector General of Police (IGP-Operations) Ch.

Srikanth, along with senior officers of Andhra Pradesh Special Police (APSP) met Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta at the Police Headquarters at Mangalagiri on Monday (November 9, 2026), and explained the operations taken up by APSDRF…
The SDRF officials explained that eleven special teams comprising 328 officers and personnel rendered services in the State from October 27 to November 1.
Rescue and relief operations were carried out in Bapatla, Konaseema, Kakinada, Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, West Godavari, East Godavari, Polavaram, and Anakapalli districts.

A total of 728 fallen trees were cleared, road clearance operations were taken up at 58 locations, and 31 electricity poles that fell on roads were removed, facilitating the movement of emergency vehicles, Mr. Srikanth said.

items.title: Six months into its rule, TVK-led government enjoys public goodwill despite concerns about it being directionless
points: Joseph Vijay handing a free travel pass to a woman at the launch of the Vettri Payanam scheme.

Photo: File | Photo Credit: ANI The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government, which completed six months in office on Monday (November 9, 2026), appears to be largely enjoying the goodwill of people, even though concerns are being raised about the…
Joseph Vijay, on his very first day in office, had declared that he had inherited an “empty coffer,” the government has been continuing with all the major welfare measures.
Reports of a “marked reduction“ in corruption regarding government appointments, transfers, and public services have impressed many observers including former Union Minister P.

In politics, where symbolism often outweighs conviction, that distinction matters.” Notwithstanding the general perception about the government‘s integrity, the two Dravidian majors — the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the All India Anna Dravida…

items.title: Man kills 4-year-old to sell his organs after watching video on making money quickly
points: Image used for representational purposes only. | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto A 27-year-old man was arrested in Chhattisgarh’s Jashpur for allegedly killing a four-year-old boy, a relative of his, with the intention to sell the boy’s organs, the…
According to the police, the man, who works as an agricultural labourer, got the idea after watching a video that purportedly suggested organ sale as a way to make money quickly.
The accused, Basudev Korwa, alias Tangnu, lives in Sanna village.
Basudev’s cousin, Ramjeet Ram, 36, also lives there with his wife and their children.
On November 5, after getting Ramjeet Ram inebriated, Basudev allegedly lured one of his sons with chicken and fed him liquor.
Jashpur Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Lal Umed Singh said the accused buried the body at a different site after extracting the organs, which he kept in a plastic bag.

items.title: Tasmac’s Deepavali sales touch ₹441 crore amid POS machine glitches
points: VELANKANNI RAJ The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) has recorded liquor sales worth ₹441.38 crore during Deepavali 2026.
According to sources, on the eve of Deepavali, Tasmac sold liquor worth over ₹234.75 crore and on the day of the festival the sales stood at ₹206.63 crore.
Chennai recorded liquor sales worth ₹95.85 crore, while the Tiruchi zone clocked ₹98.97 crore, followed by Madurai at ₹88.38 crore.
Salem reported sales of ₹87.52 crore and Coimbatore at ₹70.66 crore.
As Monday was a holiday, liquor sales are expected to remain at similar levels (sales of approximately ₹192 crore are expected).
Tasmac sources said the corporation is estimated to have collected around ₹38 crore through the Environment Protection Cess.
From November 1, 2026, a ₹10 Environmental and Social Welfare Cess was levied on liquor sales to facilitate the buy back of empty bottles.
For the year 2025-2026, Tasmac earned a revenue of ₹50,845 crore.

items.title: Upcoming IPO: Veritas Finance gets Sebi nod to launch public issue – Top things for investors
points: Veritas Finance Ltd, a non-deposit-taking non-banking financial company (NBFC), has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to launch its initial public offering (IPO), comprising a fresh issue of equity shares worth ₹900…
According to the company's latest draft red herring prospectus (DRHP), the OFS component will involve the sale of up to 1.28 crore equity shares.
The proposed public issue may also include a pre-IPO placement of specified securities worth up to ₹180 crore.
Veritas Finance had initially filed its draft IPO papers in January 2025, seeking to raise ₹2,800 crore.
That proposal comprised a fresh issue of shares worth ₹600 crore and an OFS of ₹2,200 crore.
Veritas Finance reported assets under management (AUM) of ₹9,134 crore as of March 31, 2026.
For FY26, the NBFC reported a profit of ₹330.3 crore, while its loan disbursements stood at ₹4,579.5 crore.
As of March 2026, Veritas Finance operated 444 branches, excluding service centres, across 10 states and one Union Territory.

items.title: Raptadu chainsaw attack victim’s condition improving, says A.P. Health Minister
points: Minister of Health Satya Kumar Yadav on Monday (November 9, 2026) said that the health condition of M.
Gopika, who was injured in the chainsaw attack by a youth at Raptadu ZPHS, has improved further.
The girl is currently undergoing treatment at Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru.
In an official statement here on the health condition of Gopika, the Minister said that the girl was shifted to a general ward and the medical team has changed the dressings on her wounds once again.
“Dressing has been changed for injuries on her head, neck, face, arms, and back.
Gopika has responded positively to the treatment,” the Minister said.
Mr. Satya Kumar Yadav further said that the splint on her left arm has been removed, allowing for better movement of the limb.

Earlier in the day, HRD Minister Nara Lokesh who has been monitoring the girl’s health posted on X, “The plastic surgery team completed her wound debridement and suture adjustments today without any complications.

items.title: IMO Warns of Mounting Human Toll as Attacks on Commercial Shipping Continue
points: A sailor observes the oil tanker HELGA, which is moored at one of Iraq's southern offshore oil terminals near Basra, as it prepares to load crude oil, April 24, 2026.

REUTERS/Mohammed Aty The International Maritime Organization (IMO) is calling for stronger protections for merchant ships and their crews as continued attacks in the Middle East, Red Sea and Black Sea put seafarers at risk and threaten vital shipping routes.

The warning follows the IMO Council’s 138th session in London last week, where members addressed a growing list of maritime security threats, including the war involving Iran, Houthi attacks in the Red Sea and Russian strikes on shipping and port…
According to the IMO’s latest figures, at least 130 incidents involving commercial vessels have been confirmed in the Middle East since the conflict began, with 25 seafarers now reported killed.

items.title: Broadcom shares pop over 9%, on track for biggest one-day surge in a year. What's driving the rebound?
points: Broadcom shares gained 9.5% to $321 in Monday's trade after the company announced a series of developments around its VMware business and Kubernetes ecosystem, including the acceptance of its Virtual Machine (VM) API project into the Cloud Native Computing…
The rally marked a sharp reversal from the recent sell-off and put the stock on track for its biggest single-day gain in a year.

The announcement, made at KubeCon North America, is aimed at strengthening enterprise virtualisation and cloud-native infrastructure capabilities as businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence (AI) and agentic AI workloads.
Broadcom also announced that it would co-chair the newly formed Workload Conformance Working Group within the Kubernetes community to establish common standards for running workloads on Kubernetes.
The company said more than 20 new partner solutions have been validated for VMware vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS), giving enterprise customers greater choice and flexibility.

Dilpreet Bindra, senior director of engineering at Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation Division, said modern AI and agentic workflows require virtual machines to operate within cloud-native ecosystems.

items.title: Punjab Police Brought 17 Gangsters From Abroad In Past 6 Months: AAP
points: With the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections approaching and speculation gaining momentum over a possible BJP-Akali Dal alliance, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government has stepped up its political offensive on the issue of gangsters and organised crime.

Cabinet Minister and senior AAP leader Harpal Singh Cheema on Monday claimed that Punjab Police had brought back 17 gangsters from foreign countries over the past six months, asserting that the state government had sent out a strong message that criminals…

Projecting the action as a major success of the government's 'Gangstran Te Vaar' campaign, Cheema said the police had conducted 1,61,266 raids between January 20 and November 7 and arrested around 2,162 proclaimed offenders (POs).
According to Cheema, several wanted gangsters have been brought back to India from different countries as part of coordinated international operations.

items.title: Woman's Body Chopped Into Pieces In Guwahati, Accused Arrested 6 Days Later
points: A man accused of killing a married woman with whom he had been in an extra-marital relationship for nearly a decade was arrested on Sunday, six days after the murder in Guwahati.
The accused, Pradip Taye, a resident of Dhemaji who worked as a driver in the Khanapara area of Guwahati, allegedly killed Jeena Baishya on November 1.
Her body was found in a drain near Ganesh Mandir in Khanapara on November 7.
Police said Taye and Baishya had been in a relationship for around 10 years and were living as tenants within the same residential campus.
Investigators suspect that Taye took Baishya out in his vehicle on November 1.
Around 8 pm, he allegedly took her to an isolated spot near Ganesh Mandir in Khanapara, where he attacked her with the weapon.
"The murder took place on November 1, while the woman's body was recovered from an isolated area near Ganesh Mandir in Khanapara on November 7.

items.title: From galley to kitchen: Stella Maris celebrates seafarers’ recipes
points: Maritime charity Stella Maris is celebrating the cooking skills, resourcefulness and food traditions of seafarers and fishers through a new cookbook, with all profits from the sale of the book supporting those who work at sea and their families.
The Seafarers’ Cookbook brings together recipes and personal stories from around the world, offering readers a taste of life at sea and the dishes that connect crews to home.

Published by Stella Maris and sponsored by Tindall Riley, Managers of Britannia P&I Club, the book grew from a campaign inviting seafarers to share meals that keep them going on board: breakfasts that fuel the working day, comforting dishes that bring…

Among the contributors is Richmon Dale Figueroa, whose Arroz a la Valenciana, a Filipino-style rice dish with pork and chicken, brings back memories of festivals and large gatherings during his childhood in the Philippines.

items.title: VIKING wins €23.8 million contract to build seven high-speed patrol vessels for the Hellenic Coast Guard
points: VIKING Life-Saving Equipment has signed a €23.8 million contract, through its Greek company VIKING Life-Saving Equipment Hellas, to supply seven new high-speed patrol vessels to the Hellenic Coast Guard.

The contract was signed by Greece’s Minister of Maritime Affairs and Insular Policy, Vassilis Kikilias, at a ceremony at the Ministry in Athens, attended by Coast Guard officials and VIKING representatives.
The seven vessels are of the VIKING Norsafe Magnar 1950 type and will be built entirely in Greece, one of five countries with VIKING’s manufacturing facilities.
Each vessel measures 21.29 metres in length, reaches a top speed of at least 50 knots and has a range over 320 nautical miles.
Each will operate with a six-person crew, carry at least 30 people, and be equipped with modern navigation and communication systems.
Once in service, the vessels will support the Coast Guard’s core missions: surveillance of Greek waters, protection of the country’s maritime borders, fisheries control, and search and rescue.

items.title: ONE Extends Presence in the Levant Region with new Agency Appointment in Syria
points: Ocean Network Express (ONE) has appointed Seanautics Maritime Services LLC as its official agent in Syria to support growing regional demand.
This expansion broadens ONE’s coverage across the Levant, extending its long-standing partnership with Seanautics, its established agent in Lebanon, into the Syrian market.
With offices in Damascus and Latakia, Seanautics Maritime Services LLC, present in the region for 25 years, will provide customers with direct access to ONE’s global product and services network.
Backed by local knowledge with excellent customer service, their experienced, dedicated personnel will provide direct on the ground support for ONE’s customers.

Tomohiro Hosaka, Managing Director of ONE Europe & Africa, said: “Establishing a dedicated presence in Syria is an essential step to support our customers’ growing operational and supply chain needs in the country.
With established offices in Damascus and Latakia, Seanautics brings deep insight into the local market and the practical realities of shipping in Syria.
Baconi, Deputy CEO, Seanautics Maritime Services LLC, added: Representing ONE in Syria is an exciting milestone for Seanautics.

items.title: Iran: US strikes ship after Hormuz blockade breach
points: The United States struck a commercial ship attempting to breach its naval blockade on Iran, the US military said.

According to the US Central Command (CENTCOM), the cargo vessel “tried to depart regional waters after visiting an Iranian port,” before its stern was struck by “precision munitions” shot from a US military aircraft.

In a video posted by CENTCOM, an explosion can be seen on the M/V Huda’s stern as a result of the shooting, with the ship’s civilian crew ignoring “repeated warnings.” The authorities in the UAE said 22 people had been rescued due to a fire on a vessel in…
What’s the situation in the Strait of Hormuz?
The US naval blockade on Iran, intended to pressure the country into lifting its own blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, has been in force for months.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said three “non-compliant” oil tankers caught fire while going through the Strait.

items.title: China: Arrivals up 30% MoM, iron ore futures move sideways and consolidate at highs
points: Iron ore futures shot up then pulled back today, with the most-traded DCE contract I2701 closing at 687.5 yuan/mt, up 0.07% from the previous trading day.
Spot prices for mainstream products at Qingdao Port fell by an average of about 3 yuan/mt.
Trader activity was moderate, steel mill inquiries were limited, and overall spot transactions were thin.
Supply side, according to SMM statistics, as of Nov.
6, iron ore inventory at 35 major ports nationwide stood at 149.13 million mt, up 1.08 million mt WoW.
Port arrivals fell notably this week, yet ports still saw slight inventory buildup.
Demand side, daily average port pick-up volume across the 35 ports fell 55,000 mt WoW to 3.12 million mt.
In the short term, iron ore prices may shift to consolidating at highs, a downgrade from yesterday’s slightly bullish view.

items.title: Red Sea ports handle 10,000 tons of general, miscellaneous cargo
points: The Red Sea Ports Authority said its ports handled a total of 10,000 tons of general and miscellaneous cargo, 500 trucks and 120 cars on Sunday, November 8, 2026.
Port traffic included the arrival and departure of 10 vessels, while a total of 965 passengers arrived at or departed from the ports, the authority said.
In a statement, the authority’s media center said imports involved seven vessels carrying 5,000 tons of cargo, along with 302 trucks and 114 cars.
Exports comprised six vessels carrying 5,000 tons of cargo, 198 trucks and six cars.
The statement stated that Safaga Port received the vessels POSEIDON EXPRESS and Amal, while the vessel ZHONG WANG, carrying 42,000 tons of phosphate, and the vessel PAN LILI departed the port.
Meanwhile, Nuweiba Port handled 4,900 tons of cargo and 211 trucks through round trips involving the arrival and departure of three vessels: Al-Hussein, Sina and Ayla.

items.title: US Natgas Prices Rise to Over 3-Week High
points: US natural gas prices rose more than 4% to $3.13/MMBtu on Monday, reaching their highest level since October 15, as forecasts of a sharp cold spell pointed to stronger heating demand.

More than 160 million Americans could face below-average temperatures by November 14, a significant reversal from the unusually warm conditions expected earlier in the week, particularly across the Northeast, Great Lakes and Ohio Valley.
Supply-side factors also supported prices, with the latest EIA report showing a smaller-than-expected storage build of 77 Bcf for the week ended October 30.
Inventories reached 3.801 trillion cubic feet, remaining 2.8% below year-earlier levels but 1.4% above the five-year average.
Meanwhile, Lower 48 production averaged 111.2 Bcf per day in November, down from October’s 113.4 Bcf.
LNG export flows also eased slightly, although international demand for US shipments remains strong amid ongoing geopolitical disruptions to global energy supplies.

items.title: US Consumer Inflation Expectations Steady at 3.9%
points: Median US inflation expectations for the year ahead were steady at 3.9% in October 2026, the same as in September, and holding at 2023-highs, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s Survey of Consumer Expectations.
Median year-ahead expected price changes decreased by 0.6 pp to 4.2% for gas and were unchanged at 5.5% for food.
In contrast, price changes increased by 0.1 pp to 9.3% for the cost of medical care, by 0.1 pp to 7.6% for the cost of college education, and by 0.9 pp to 7.7% for rent.
Median home price growth expectations were unchanged at 3%, just below its 12-month trailing average of 3.1%.
Meanwhile, expectations for the three-year and five-year horizons were also steady at 3.3% and 3% respectively.

Elsewhere, earnings growth expectations remained unchanged at 2.6%, unemployment expectations rose by 1.4 pp to 45.3%, its highest reading since April 2020 and expected growth in household income declined by 0.1 pp to 3%.

items.title: Disha higher education exhibition draws large crowds in Malappuram
points: Students in front of a stall at Disha higher education exhibition at MSP Parade Ground, Malappuram, on Monday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN The Disha higher education exhibition being held at the MSP Parade Ground here drew large crowds of school…
Secondary and higher secondary students from schools across Malappuram and neighbouring districts arrived in groups, crowding the stalls.
Around 80 institutions in the government sector are participating in the five-day exhibition.
The exhibition also provides information on the Kerala Differential Aptitude Test (K-DAT), developed by the Higher Secondary wing of the General Education department.

items.title: Mamata Banerjee Gets Delhi Police Notice To Record Statement In 2013 Case
points: Delhi Police has issued a fresh notice to former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee to record her statement as a 'victim' in a 2013 case related to a protest by SFI and CPI(M) supporters during her visit to the national capital, officials said on…
A team of Delhi Police is currently in Kolkata to facilitate the process, and Banerjee's statement will be recorded by the Parliament Street police station, police sources said.
The notice has been issued to Banerjee in her capacity as a victim in the case, and not as an accused, they clarified.
The case pertains to an incident in April 2013, when Banerjee, who was then the West Bengal chief minister, visited the former Planning Commission headquarters in Delhi for an official meeting.
During her visit, SFI and CPI(M) supporters allegedly raised slogans against her, leading to a fight with the members of her delegation.

items.title: 4,500 vs 34,000: NASA Scientist Flags Punjab-Haryana Farm Fires Undercount
points: In Punjab, where governments have repeatedly claimed progress in the fight against stubble burning, the number of farm fires recorded by official agencies stands at 4,459 this season.

Dr Hiren Jethva, an aerosol remote sensing scientist associated with Morgan State University and NASA's Goddard Space Flight Centre, stated that his calculations showed 34,000 farm fires in Punjab and Haryana between October 1 and November 9 this year.
The estimate is dramatically higher than the 4,459 incidents recorded by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) up to Sunday.
1–Nov 9) Punjab+Haryana 🛰️ NOAA-20 VIIRS (375 m): 4,089 fires near 1:30 p.m.

LT 🔥 After empirical adjustment to VIIRS 375 m fire-count baseline, the total reaches to ~34,000 fires--a conservative estimate According to the CAQM's report covering the period up to November 8, Punjab recorded 4,459 incidents of stubble burning this season.

items.title: Rape-Accused Trinamool Congress MLA Arrested At Kolkata Airport
points: On-the-run Trinamool Congress (TMC) legislator Paresh Ram Das, the MLA representing Canning (Paschim) in South 24 Parganas district, was arrested at the Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport in Kolkata on Monday evening while allegedly…

Das, an accused in a high-profile rape and extortion case, had been evading law enforcement for 17 days and repeatedly failed to respond to summons issued by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of the West Bengal Police.
A special operations group from the Baruipur Police District, acting on specific intelligence, tracked Das to the airport and apprehended him with assistance from the Bidhannagar City Police.
The joint operation was conducted under the direct supervision of the Superintendent of Police, Bidhannagar Police District.
The investigation originates from a complaint filed in September this year with the Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) of Canning.
The victim alleged that before the 2023 panchayat elections, Das demanded Rs 4 lakh from her husband under the pretext of securing an election ticket.

items.title: Video: Lucknow Petrol Pump Employee Dragged By Car As Driver Flees Without Paying
points: A petrol pump employee was dragged after he tried to stop the driver of a car from fleeing without paying in Lucknow's Gosaiganj area.
The incident happened on the morning of November 8 at around 4:19 am at the GS Petrol Pump near Sainik Dhaba.
A man in a black car got his fuel tank refilled at the petrol station and tried to speed off without payment.
CCTV footage of the incident shows a petrol pump employee grabbing the car door to stop the vehicle from fleeing, following which, the driver accelerated and dragged him along for a distance.
The employee, identified as 21-year-old Sachin Kumar, sustained injuries in the incident.
The petrol pump manager filed a complaint, after which a case was registered under relevant sections at the Gosaiganj police station.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Md Mushtaq has constituted three police teams to crack the case and arrest the accused.

items.title: Police seize third video allegedly showing ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani abusing minor
points: Veeramani and his close associates are facing seven cases under the POCSO Act and a case relating to the abetment of the suicide of a minor in 2004. | Photo Credit: B.
JOTHI RAMALINGAM The Greater Chennai Police have seized one more video purportedly showing Gem Granites owner R.
Veeramani sexually abusing a minor girl, taking the total number of such videos recovered in the case to three, police sources said on Monday.
Besides Veeramani, Shanthi and her husband Mahendra Simhan, six other accused persons have so far been arrested in eight different cases and lodged in the Puzhal Central Prison.

The businessman and his close associates are facing seven cases under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and a case relating to the abetment of the suicide of a minor in 2004.
The transactions reportedly took place around the time Veeramani sold two parcels of land along the East Coast Road for a total consideration of about ₹80 crore, the sources said.

items.title: U.S. Container Imports Hit 2026 High in September as Extended Peak Season Winds Down
points: A CMA CGM containerships waits at anchor outside the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach.

Photo courtesy Port of Los Angeles U.S. container imports reached their highest level of the year in September, capping an unusually long peak shipping season that has kept major ports busy since the spring despite tariffs, inflation and growing pressure…

Ports covered by the National Retail Federation (NRF) and Hackett Associates’ Global Port Tracker handled 2.37 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) of loaded imports in September, up 12.6% from a year earlier and 3.4% from August.
The total made September the third-busiest month since Global Port Tracker began keeping records, trailing only July 2025’s 2.39 million TEUs and May 2022’s 2.4 million TEUs.

Hackett Associates founder Ben Hackett said the import surge that began in 2025 appeared to be winding down earlier this year after the Supreme Court struck down the Trump administration’s sweeping “Liberation Day” tariffs.

items.title: India-EU review FTA progress ahead of PM Modi's Brussels visit, push investment and trade ties
points: India and the European Union (EU) on Monday reviewed efforts aimed at the timely signing and implementation of a free trade agreement and to conclude an investment protection agreement and an agreement on geographical indications.

These matters figured at an India-EU strategic partnership review meeting held in New Delhi, weeks ahead of an expected visit by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Brussels in mid-December for the signing of the FTA.

India and the EU reviewed engagements aimed at boosting trade and investment cooperation, including the “timely signing and implementation of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement”, and to conclude the investment protection agreement and the agreement on…

The two sides expressed satisfaction at deepening research collaboration, including India’s potential association with Horizon Europe, the EU’s €93.5-billion flagship research and innovation programme.
Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015.

items.title: Four acres of encroached land reclaimed in Ballari; task force clears 150 acres
points: The demolition was carried out following allegations of encroachment on government land.
According to the district administration, 1 acre and 9 guntas of land in survey number 607/ 1A had been encroached upon and enclosed by a compound wall.
The administration removed the structure as part of its drive to reclaim government land and public roads.
In a related development, the government has also reclaimed 2 acres and 30 guntas of land allotted to the Arogya Niketan Trust in the same survey number 14 years ago.
The land had been allotted for the welfare of underprivileged children and children with disabilities.
As per the conditions of the allotment, the land was required to be utilised for the intended purpose within two years.
With these measures, the district administration has reclaimed approximately four acres of government land in the survey number.

Additional Deputy Commissioner Mohammed Zubair said that the district-level task force constituted to identify and clear encroachments on government land has reclaimed approximately 150 acres across the district so far.

items.title: Bihar govt bans firecrackers near ghats, private boat operations during Chhath Puja
points: The Bihar Disaster Management Department has directed all districts to enforce strict safety measures during Chhath Puja (November 13-16), including a ban on firecrackers near ghats and private boat operations, officials said.
According to a statement issued by the department on Monday, district magistrates have been asked to identify and barricade dangerous ghats, and deploy adequate security personnel and volunteers.
It has also directed that trained divers, swimmers, motorboats and life-saving equipment be stationed at river ghats.
Medical teams, ambulances and Quick Medical Response Teams (QMRTs) must remain on standby, the statement said.
The directives also call for adequate lighting at ghats and approach roads, round-the-clock functioning of district control rooms and continuous public announcements through loudspeakers.

To prevent panic and stampedes, district magistrates have been asked to prepare disaster management and communication plans, hold coordination meetings with Chhath committees and ensure strict monitoring throughout the festival.
The four-day festival will begin on November 13 with the 'Nahai Khai' ritual and conclude on November 16.

items.title: Experts Explain Why Delhi's Air Quality Monitors Went Blank On Diwali Night
points: Similar gaps were reported at Nehru Nagar, Mundka, Sonia Vihar and Dwarka.

An analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) found that the number of stations not reporting readings rose from seven at 10 pm on November 8 to 23 at 11 pm, 29 at midnight and 36 at 1 am on November 9.

items.title: Keralam Excise dept. bans issuance of new liquor licences until promulgation of Keralam govt.’s liquor policy

Additional Excise Commissioner (Enforcement) R Jayasankar, who holds the charge of Excise Commissioner, barred Deputy Commissioners from issuing new bar licences, including permits for beer and wine parlours that have acquired four-star hotel…

Bengaluru to host first meet of Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians‘ regional unit
points: A special convention of the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians’ Indian Regional Unit will be held in Bengaluru on November 17 and 18.
Announcing this at a press conference in Bengaluru on Monday, Assembly Speaker G.S.
Patil and Legislative Council Chairman Salim Ahmed said such a convention, which was being held for the first time in the country, would be inaugurated by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.
The convention is being jointly organised by the Indian Parliament and the Karnataka legislature, they said.
About 150 women MPs, women presiding officers of legislative Houses and women legislators from different States are expected to participate in the convention, they noted.
The convention will deliberate on issues related to online harassment of women elected representatives, including false propaganda through fake accounts and cybercrimes, he said.

Mr. Patil maintained that the Bengaluru convention would be an important initiative in the country’s parliamentary history as it would bring together women MPs and legislators on a common platform to discuss issues related to their participation in the…

items.title: Legal awareness rally held to mark National Legal Services Day
points: The District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) organised an awareness rally and a meeting in Visakhapatnam on Monday to mark National Legal Services Day, as part of the Action Plan 2025-26 of the Andhra Pradesh State Legal Services Authority, Amaravati.
DLSA chairman and Principal District Judge G.
Srinivas flagged off the rally at 9.30 a.m. from Nyaya Seva Sadan.
At the meeting that followed, he said the Authority’s aim was to provide legal justice to the economically and socially disadvantaged, and that no one should be denied justice because of poverty.
Legal aid clinics, panel advocates and para-legal volunteers would offer free services and advice across the district, he said, urging people to make use of them.
Sanyasi Naidu, Visakhapatnam Bar Association president Nammi Sanyasi Rao, and A.P.
Bar Council members Krishna Mohan and B.V.R.
Judicial officers, legal aid defence counsel, panel advocates, para-legal volunteers and court staff took part.

items.title: India gets quota of 1.75 lakh pilgrims under Saudi Arabia's Haj 2027 agreement
points: India and Saudi Arabia on Monday signed the bilateral Haj agreement for 2027, under which 1,75,025 Indians will be allowed to undertake the annual pilgrimage, the Indian Consulate in Jeddah said.

Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju, who is on an official visit to Saudi Arabia, held a bilateral meeting with Saudi Minister of Hajj and Umrah Tawfiq bin Fawzan Al Rabiah before signing the agreement in Jeddah.

"The Ministers reviewed the ongoing preparations for Haj-2027, discussed measures to strengthen bilateral coordination and logistical support, and reaffirmed their shared commitment to a safe, smooth and comfortable pilgrimage for Indian Haj pilgrims," the…
India's Haj quota has increased over the years, from 1,36,020 in 2014 to 1,75,025 for 2025, according to the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
Rijiju, accompanied by Joint Secretary (Haj) Mohammad Afzal, is on a visit to Saudi Arabia from November 6 to 9.

items.title: Trump administration's embrace of "perp" futures sets off risk alarms for Wall Street stalwarts
points: The decision by the Trump administration to launch perpetual futures has sparked significant worry among market stakeholders.
Leaders from established exchanges contend that these offerings might disrupt existing market dynamics and risk assessment practices.
They claim that perpetual futures ought to be categorized as swaps due to their unique trading characteristics.
Moreover, ongoing trading raises alarm about liquidity and counterparty risk, especially in turbulent market conditions.

items.title: 13 years on, Delhi Police serve notice on Mamata Banerjee in 2013 protest case
points: According to police officials, a team of Delhi police visited Ms. Banerjee’s residence on Harish Chatterjee Street in Kolkata's Kalighat to serve the notice.
"The notice was served under Section 160 of the Indian Penal Code in connection with case no 57/13 dated April 9, 2013.
The case was registered at New Delhi's Parliament Street Police Station under sections 186, 353, 332,147,149, 34 of IPC," the police said in a statement.
The 2013 gherao of Banga Bhawan was part of a major student agitation in New Delhi triggered by the death of 22-year-old SFI leader Sudipto Gupta in police custody in Kolkata.
On April 3, 2013, hundreds of SFI and Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) protesters stormed and gheraoed Banga Bhawan, the official West Bengal government guest house on Hailey Road.

ALSO WATCH Watch: Abhishek Banerjee alleges BJP supporters attacked his Kolkata residence Tensions escalated on April 9, 2013, outside the Planning Commission office, where the then West Bengal Finance Minister Amit Mitra and Ms. Banerjee had arrived for…

items.title: Police mull joint interrogation of accused in Abhiram murder case
points: Published - November 09, 2026 10:25 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The Special Investigation Team probing the murder of 17-year old Abhiram in Pangappara is reportedly planning to interrogate the first accused, a 17-year-old juvenile, and the second accused,…
Umar and the third accused, Ananda, who were taken into police custody on October 7, were returned to judicial remand on Monday.
Umar is likely to be taken into custody again for questioning.
The police have also approached the Juvenile Justice Board to obtain the custody of the prime accused.
During evidence collection conducted at the crime scene on Sunday, Umar told media persons that he had been framed in the case.
He also claimed that he did not know Abhiram or his friends.
However, police maintained that the accused was attempting to mislead the investigation.
The first and second accused have reportedly provided conflicting accounts regarding the whereabouts of Abhiram’s mobile phone and the belt allegedly used in the murder.

items.title: Remain accessible to people, Visakhapatnam MP tells Corporators
points: Sribharat along with Mayor Mukka Sravani and Corporators of GVMC who won in the recent elections, at his party office in Visakhapatnam on Monday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Visakhapatnam MP M.

Sribharat has called upon the newly elected TDP Corporators to dedicate their victory in the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) elections to the people and remain accessible to them at all times, sharing their joys and hardships.

The newly elected TDP Corporators from Visakhapatnam South – Majji Trinath Rao (Ward 35), Urukuti Narayana Rao (Ward 30), Akkireddy Jagadeesh (Ward 45), Pukkalla Rajeswari (Ward 38), and Golagani Jyothi (Ward 44) – met Mr. Sribharat at his office on…
They paid a courtesy visit to the MP and shared their happiness over the victory in the recent GVMC elections.
Addressing the Corporators who met him, the MP stressed the importance of maintaining close coordination and cordial relations with all Corporators of the Alliance.

items.title: AMD stock rallies 12% as Google Cloud taps its EPYC processors for next-generation AI infrastructure
points: Shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) extended their recovery for a second consecutive session on Monday, November 9, surging 12.5% to an intraday high of $504.80 apiece.
The rally came after the Nvidia rival announced that its fifth-generation EPYC server processors would power Alphabet's Google Cloud TPU 8tx systems.

The collaboration brings together AMD's EPYC central processing units (CPUs), Infinity Guard security capabilities, and x86 software compatibility with Google's TPU AI acceleration technology, as per company's release.
Under the deployment, AMD said that it fifth-generation EPYC processors will manage workload orchestration, data preparation, and high-throughput communication with Google's TPU accelerators.
The system uses AMD's Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) technology alongside Google's TPU architecture to extend confidential computing protection beyond the CPU to connected accelerators.
He added that AMD has developed performance, memory bandwidth, and input/output capabilities across generations of EPYC processors, backed by engineering collaborations with leading cloud providers.

items.title: Telangana High Court sentences Ranga Reddy Collector to six months’ imprisonment for wilful disobedience in a contempt case
points: The Telangana High Court awarded six-month imprisonment to Ranga Reddy district Collector C.
Narayana Reddy in a contempt of court case.
Lakshman of the High Court, pronouncing the punishment holding the IAS officer guilty of wilful disobedience of the HC order, also imposed a fine of ₹2,000 on the Collector.
The contempt of court case was filed by a housewife P.

Venkateshwarlu stating that the Collector wilfully disobeyed an order passed by the HC in 2025 while disposing of their writ petition seeking a direction to issue No Objection Certificate for their open plots at Turkayamjal in Ranga Reddy district.
On August 5 last year, the HC passed an order instructing the Collector to consider the representation of the couple for deleting their plots from list of prohibitory properties.
The Collector should pass a reasoned order if he was not inclined to accept the request of the couple and communicate the same to them within 60 days, the order said.

items.title: Karnataka CM to hold meeting next week on issues faced by minorities
points: Shivakumar on Monday announced that he would hold a meeting next week to hear and resolve issues faced by minorities.

Inaugurating the “Jashn-e-Urdu” programme organised by the Karnataka Urdu Academy to present annual awards and release books, the Chief Minister said, “Discussions will be held with leaders and legislators representing various minority communities,…

Additionally, the views and issues of SC and ST legislators will also be heard.” “Fulfilling the promises made in our manifesto during the elections and the commitments given to communities on various occasions is our responsibility.
Meetings are being held to resolve issues respectfully without hurting anyone’s sentiments.
“Some people may not have faith in minority communities.
But just because others lack faith, the Minorities Welfare Department cannot be shut down.
On the occasion, the Chief Minister assured the gathering that more grants would be allocated for the activities of the Urdu Academy.

items.title: Chhattisgarh man kills 4-year-old relative, removes organs to sell online
points: A 27-year-old man allegedly murdered his four-year-old relative in Jashpur district of Chhattisgarh and removed his kidneys, lungs and eyes to sell them online after being influenced by social media, police said on Sunday.
The accused, identified as Basudev alias Tangnu, was arrested after the child's body was found stuffed in a sack and dumped in a pit in Lodhenapath Mahua village, Jashpur district, police said.
The victim, Jitendra Ram, had been missing since November 5.
His father, Ramjeet Ram (36), lodged a missing complaint at Sanna police station on Saturday, Jashpur Senior Superintendent of Police Lal Umed Singh said.
Ramjeet had moved with his family to Sanna village about a year ago in search of work and lived in a hut near the Aamatchua river dam.

While searching for the child with family members on Saturday, Ramjeet found his son's body stuffed in a sack, wrapped in a blanket and quilt, and partially buried in a water-filled pit near a maize field.

items.title: Bengaluru: Firecracker injuries threaten vision; two infants among victims
points: Shabnam undergoing medical care at Minto Eye Hospital after a firecracker accident during Deepavali celebrations severely damaged her eye, in Bengaluru on November 9, 2026. | Photo Credit: K.
MURALI KUMAR Firecracker-related eye injuries continue to take the sparkle out of the festival of lights, with several people facing the risk of partial or near-total vision loss this Deepavali too.
Children, including infants as young as three and five months, are among those affected, while bystanders account for a significant share of the victims.
At the State-run Minto Ophthalmic Hospital, 12 of the 20 patients treated over the three days till November 9 suffered grievous injuries.
Significantly, 13 were bystanders who were watching others burst crackers or happened to be nearby.
A 12-year-old boy from Doddaballapur suffered a ruptured eyeball after being hit by a firecracker burst by another person and is at risk of partial vision loss.

items.title: Srisailam gears up for ‘Karthika Masam’ festivities from November 10
points: The Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple in Srisailam is all decked up for the auspicious ‘Karthika Masam’ festivities. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT The month-long ‘Karthika Masam’ festivities at Sri Bhramarmba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple in Srisailam…
Meanwhile, ‘Laksha Deepotsavam’ (lighting of one hundred thousand lamps) and ‘Pushkarini Harati’ (ritual offering of lamps at the temple tank) will be conducted every Monday during the month.
Temple Trust Board chairman Pothugunta Ramesh Naidu and executive officer (EO) M.
Srinivasa Rao said in a press release on Monday that ‘Sparsha Darshan’ will be suspended on Saturdays, Sundays, Mondays, and other auspicious festival days.
On regular days, Sparsha Darshan will be permitted during specific time slots to ensure there is no inconvenience to devotees in the ‘Sarva Darshanam’ (general queue) line.
The temple doors will open daily at 3 a.m.
After the early morning rituals, darshan will be available from 4.30 a.m. until 4 p.m., after which it will resume at 5.30 p.m.

items.title: Post-Diwali air pollution adds to respiratory distress, Noida doctors report rise in hospital visits
points: Delhi and neighbouring Noida woke up to toxic air on Monday, a day after Diwali, as firecracker emissions added to the national capital's already poor air quality.
Around 80% of operational monitoring stations recorded 'severe' air quality between 10pm on Diwali and 6am the following morning, HT had reported earlier.

As of the latest 9pm update, Noida's air quality index (AQI) stood at 327, placing it in the 'very poor' category, HT Pollution Dashboard, which tracks average readings from all monitoring stations reported by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB),…
At Fortis Hospital in Noida’s Sector 62, pulmonologists are seeing 20-30 new patients daily with allergic airway diseases, asthma exacerbations, persistent cough, wheezing and breathlessness.
At Yatharth Hospital in Noida’s Sector 110, four such cases were reported on Monday, according to Dr Arunachalam M, senior consultant and head of pulmonology.

items.title: Akhilesh’s proposed Ayodhya visit to broaden his PDA outreach, say political analysts
points: Samajwadi Party National President Akhilesh Yadav.

Analysts see the visit as attempts by the SP chief to leave no stone unturned before Assembly polls early next year and addressing the concerns of Brahmins, who are traditionally associated with temple priesthood.
Party spokesperson Pawan Pandey last week said that Mr. Yadav will go to Hanuman Garhi with his MP wife Dimple Yadav and other family members and later to the Ram Temple on December 12.

“Akhilesh Yadav ji made it clear several times that religion and faith are personal issues, and he will visit [Lord] Ramlalla in Ayodhya after the completion of the Kedareshwar temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and situated on the same latitude as the…
Let them apologise once to devotees and once to the saints,” said Mr. Adityanath, addressing the 10th edition of Deepotsav in Ayodhya on November 7.
Akhilesh Yadav is aware that in the 2022 Assembly polls, despite getting a sizeable vote share, he was far from forming the government.

items.title: China Extends US Trade Truce by Two Months
points: FILE PHOTO: A drone view shows a cargo ship at Kwai Tsing Container Terminals in Hong Kong, China, April 16, 2025.

REUTERS/Tyrone Siu TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY/File Photo BEIJING, Nov 9 (Reuters) – China on Monday effectively extended its trade truce with the US by two months, after announcing it would continue to suspend certain trade measures.

The trade truce was due to expire on Tuesday, with Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump expected to meet, for the third time so far this year, at the APEC leaders’ summit in China next week.

After September’s Washington summit between Trump and Xi, both sides proposed a $60-billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts, including roughly $17 billion worth of US farm goods that China imported in 2024, though the plan has yet to be finalized.

items.title: Six, including sarpanch, injured in stray dog attack in Rekonda village of Karimnagar district
points: Around six persons were injured, one of them grievously, when a stray dog went on a biting spree at Rekonda village in Chigurumamidi mandal of Karimnagar district on Monday.
According to sources, a stray dog went berserk and attacked an elderly woman who was sitting in front of her house in the afternoon.
She sustained bleeding injuries to her legs.
The dog subsequently attacked several other people passing through the street, inflicting multiple injuries on them.
The local sarpanch reportedly attempted to chase the dog away but sustained an injury to his leg.
The injured were shifted to the Government General Hospital in Karimnagar for treatment.
The incident triggered panic among residents of Rekonda, who demanded immediate measures to control the stray dog menace in and around the village.

items.title: A.P. cities record dip in AQI after Deepavali; Visakhapatnam worst hit
points: Fireworks illuminate the night sky amid thick clouds of smoke along Beach Road in Visakhapatnam on Sunday, as people celebrate Deepavali. | Photo Credit: K.R.
DEEPAK People in Andhra Pradesh celebrated Deepavali emphatically with firecrackers illuminating the night skies, leaving the air quality deteriorated and making it harder to breathe on Monday.

While all prominent cities in the State recorded “moderate” air quality, ranging between 101 and 200, air in Visakhapatnam and Rajamahendravaram dipped to the “poor” category on Monday, according to the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board (APPCB).
On Deepavali last year, October 20, Visakhapatnam recorded an AQI of 44.

Krishnaiah, Chairman, APPCB, said the 72 manual and 20 continuous monitoring stations across the State ordinarily record air and noise levels within permitted limits, but the burning of crackers during Deepavali pushed pollution up.
Real-time noise monitoring recorded peak levels of 111 dB(A) in Visakhapatnam and 112 dB(A) in Vijayawada on Deepavali night, against the night-time standard of 45 dB(A) for residential areas.

items.title: Karnataka govt stands by report of over 20% ethanol in petrol, questions oil firms' data on blending
points: Talking to reporters, the minister for food, civil supplies, consumer affairs and legal metrology said the government will not withdraw its findings that OMCs were blending more than the prescribed 20% ethanol in petrol, with some samples showing levels of…

“The Government of Karnataka stands by its report and claims that oil marketing companies are blending more than 20% ethanol in petrol, which will cause serious damage to the engines of vehicles and burden the common man,” he said.
The minister also demanded that consumers be given the choice of buying E10, E20, E30 and pure petrol, depending on their vehicles’ compatibility.

The findings recorded an Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) sample with 31.2% ethanol, while samples from Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) recorded 30.5% and 26.5%, respectively.
They cited a separate exercise in which 893 samples from 27 states and Union territories, including 56 from Karnataka, were found to contain between 19% and 21% ethanol.

points: A file photo of the Shiradi Ghat stretch on Bengaluru-Mangaluru National Highway 75.

Image for representational purposes only. | Photo Credit: ANIL KUMAR SASTRY In a significant development in the case of the murders of seven members of a family, which has sent shockwaves across Karnataka, the police have now successfully recovered all…
The latest breakthrough came on Monday (November 9, 2026), with the police recovering two more bodies from Shiradi Ghat, in the Western Ghats of Karnataka.
The development comes a day after the police recovered two bodies of the accused’s brother-in-law, Shivakumar and his wife, Divya, from the foothills of Chamundi Hills on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
On November 6, they had recovered the body of a minor boy, Puneeth, 7, from the foothills of Nandi Hills.

items.title: Congress government paying ₹80,000 crore per year for debts left behind by KCR: Revanth
points: Revanth Reddy along with his Cabinet colleagues participating in a padayatra from the Pollepally Yellamma temple to the public meeting venue at Lagacharla in Kodangal on Monday (November 9, 2026).

Revanth Reddy yet again targeted Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) chief K Chandrashekhar Rao, claiming the latter had done grave injustice to Telangana, raising loans indiscriminately, forcing the current Congress government to pay ₹80,000 crore every year…
“More than ₹2 lakh crore has been paid in the last 34 months for the ₹8.11 lakh crore debts left behind by the KCR government.
₹80,000 crore has to be repaid every year,” he said while addressing a public meeting titled ‘Raithannatho Atmeeya Sabha’ at the Lagacharla Industrial Corridor on Monday (November 09).

items.title: US dollar dips as easing AI and Mideast worries limit its appeal
points: After a six-month high, the US dollar is now on a downward trend, largely spurred by impressive job growth figures.
Investors are eagerly awaiting the upcoming consumer price index data, a key factor for Federal Reserve rate considerations.
Meanwhile, the euro and other currencies are rebounding against the dollar, backed by solid economic indicators.

items.title: ‘This is New Delhi’: Chinese vloggers misrepresent Dhaka streets in online streams
points: An online misinformation operation being run from Bangladesh has come under scrutiny after reports emerged of Chinese content creators using footage recorded in some of Dhaka’s economically disadvantaged neighbourhoods to misrepresent conditions in New Delhi.

According to Bangladeshi media reports, these individuals reportedly streamed videos of local streets while claiming they were filmed in Delhi and making derogatory remarks on the area’s living standards.

The scale of the activity came to light following an investigation by Bangladeshi newspaper Prothom Alo, which identified at least 150 Chinese nationals recording videos in Dhaka's Tekpara and Uttara localities.
To verify the content of the broadcasts, the report used Google Translate to convert selected portions of the Chinese-language streams into English.
As per the translation published in the Bangladeshi media report, a Chinese woman identified as Mianmian told viewers, "This is New Delhi.
Attempts to understand the intentions of the Chinese nationals led a group of Bangladeshi journalists to visit the area on October 27 and November 3.

items.title: SS United States Set for Final Voyage Ahead of Historic Sinking Off Florida
points: The SS United States, a retired American ocean liner, that was built during 1950 and 1951 for United States Lines, is towed out to sea on the Delaware River, on her way to Alabama where she is intended to be sunk to create an artificial reef, in…

REUTERS/Matthew Hatcher The historic SS United States, once the fastest ocean liner in the world, is scheduled to leave Mobile, Alabama, on Monday for its final voyage before being intentionally sunk off Florida’s Gulf Coast later this week.

The 990-foot vessel is scheduled to become the world’s largest artificial reef when it is scuttled on Thursday, about 22 nautical miles southwest of Destin-Fort Walton Beach, according to Okaloosa County officials.
The U.S. Coast Guard has established a temporary 100-yard moving safety zone around the vessel and its towing vessels for the transit out of Mobile Bay.

items.title: Höegh Autoliners Taps BYD Battery Technology for Ammonia-Powered Car Carrier
points: Höegh Autoliners has signed an agreement with Chinese battery manufacturer BYD to install a marine battery system aboard its upcoming Aurora No. 12 car carrier, combining battery storage, solar panels and a shaft generator with ammonia propulsion.
The agreement, signed Monday at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, will see the vessel equipped with an integrated energy system designed to reduce fuel consumption and emissions.
Scheduled for delivery in May 2028, Aurora No. 12 will be capable of operating on ammonia from the day it leaves the shipyard.
Aurora No. 12 is part of Höegh Autoliners’ expanding Aurora-class newbuilding program at China Merchants Heavy Industry in China.
Each vessel can carry up to 9,100 cars, with the company claiming carbon emissions per vehicle transported can be reduced by as much as 58% compared with conventional car carriers.
The latest development follows Höegh Autoliners’ August order for six additional Aurora-class vessels, bringing the program to 18 ships.

items.title: How In-Water Services Are Optimizing Vessel & Infrastructure Repair
points: For many vessel owners, a problem below the waterline used to mean one answer: get the ship out of the water.
This time intensive process consisted of booking a drydock slot, repositioning the vessel and waiting for a full assessment.
In the case of underwater infrastructure, the tooling lacked the technological advances available today and many fixes were complex and time consuming.
Now, a growing share of the inspection, maintenance and repair that once required a dry hull can be done in-water by commercial divers.
Today it is governed by AWS D3.6M, the industry’s underwater welding code.
Commercial divers now handle sophisticated construction and repair these assets in water.
They cut and remove piles and pile caps, take down and reinstall mooring dolphins and catwalks, and seal and internally plug pipelines.
Ultrasonic thickness gauging maps plate wastage across the hull.
